record.title: Grötzsch's conjecture on edge-coloring subcubic planar graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a $2$-connected planar graph with maximum degree $\Delta(G)\leq 3$. **Grötzsch's conjecture.** The graph $G$ is $3$-edge-colorable unless it has exactly one vertex of degree $2$.

A $2$-connected subcubic graph with exactly one degree-$2$ vertex is not $3$-edge-colorable, so the conjecture asserts that this is the only obstruction for planar graphs. If true, it would put the planar $3$-Edge Colorability problem in $\P$, since the condition is checkable in linear time; the conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Miriam Goetze, Paul Jungeblut and Torsten Ueckerdt, “Efficient Recognition of Subgraphs of Planar Cubic Bridgeless Graphs”, arXiv:2204.11750 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.11750

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2022).

record.title: Luo, Tian and Wu's connectivity-preserving tree conjecture for bipartite graphs
record.statement:
Let $T$ be a tree with bipartition $X$ and $Y$, and set

$$
t=\max\{|X|,|Y|\}.
$$

Let $G$ be a $k$-connected bipartite graph with minimum degree $\delta(G)\geq k+t$. **Luo, Tian and Wu's conjecture.** The graph $G$ contains a subtree $T'\cong T$ such that

$$
\kappa(G-V(T'))\geq k.
$$

This conjecture is a bipartite analogue of Mader's conjecture on deleting a prescribed tree while preserving connectivity. The paper confirms it for caterpillars when $k=3$ and for spiders when $k\leq 3$, while the general case remains open.
record.source_name: Qing Yang and Yingzhi Tian, “Connectivity keeping caterpillars and spiders in bipartite graphs with connectivity at most three”, arXiv:2205.00397 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.00397

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2022).

record.title: Reineke's total stability conjecture for Dynkin quivers
record.statement: Let $Q$ be a finite Dynkin quiver and let $A=KQ$ be its path algebra. A **slope function** is a map $\mu:K_0(A)\setminus\{0\}\to\mathbb{R}$ of the form $\mu=\frac{\theta}{\kappa}$, where $\theta$ and $\kappa$ are linear functions on $K_0(A)$ and $\kappa(M)>0$ for every nonzero $M\in K_0(A)$. A slope function defines a **total stability condition** if every indecomposable $A$-module is $\mu$-stable. Here $\dim$ denotes the function assigning to a module its dimension over the base field. **Reineke's total stability conjecture.** There exists a slope function of the form $\mu=\frac{\theta}{\dim}$ that defines a total stability condition for $A$. The conjecture is refuted: a path algebra of Dynkin type $E_7$ with a specific orientation admits no slope function of this form defining a total stability condition, providing a counterexample to the conjecture.
record.source_name: Rene Marczinzik, “On total stability conditions for Dynkin quivers”, arXiv:2205.00947 (2022).
record.references:
**4 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2011–2022). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2202.00092](https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.00092), [arXiv:1804.09100](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.09100), [arXiv:1111.1010](https://arxiv.org/abs/1111.1010).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.00947

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of May 2022).

record.title: Przytycki's freeness conjecture for non-Haken 3-manifolds
record.statement: Let $M$ be a closed, oriented, irreducible $3$-manifold. A manifold is **non-Haken** when it contains no embedded oriented incompressible surfaces. **Przytycki's conjecture.** The following increasingly weaker assertions are conjectured: (1) the Kauffman bracket skein module of every closed, prime, oriented $3$-manifold decomposes as a direct sum of free modules and torsion modules; (2) the same holds for every closed, irreducible, atoroidal, oriented $3$-manifold; and (3) the Kauffman bracket skein module of every closed, oriented, irreducible, non-Haken $3$-manifold is torsion-free, hence free. The source says that the author presents a counterexample to Marché's conjecture but records these weaker structural claims as conjectures; the final assertion is related to a conjecture of Przytycki and to the finite-dimensionality theorem over $d412(A)$.
record.source_name: Rhea Palak Bakshi, “A Counterexample to the Generalisation of Witten's Conjecture”, arXiv:2205.01653 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.01653

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of May 2022). “While writing , the author discovered a counterexample to this conjecture given by the KBSM of the connected sum of real projective spaces.”

record.title: The singular orbit conjecture for trinomial hypersurfaces
record.statement: Let $X$ be a trinomial hypersurface, and let ${\mathbb T}$ act on $X$ by the torus action considered in the paper. Singular orbits are points or subsets of $X$ consisting entirely of singular points. **The singular orbit conjecture.** All singular $\operatorname{Aut}_{alg}(X)$-orbits of $X$ coincide with ${\mathbb T}$-orbits. This would determine when linked torus orbits can be glued by algebraic automorphisms; the claim is proved in the paper when all exponents $l_{ij}$ are at least $2$, but is left open in general.
record.source_name: Sergey Gaifullin and Georgiy Shirinkin, “Orbits of automorphism group of trinomial hypersurfaces”, arXiv:2205.02513 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.02513

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2022).

record.title: The independence–dissociation bound for connected triangle-free subcubic graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected triangle-free subcubic graph. Write $calpha(G)$ for its independence number and ${\rm diss}(G)$ for its dissociation number, the maximum cardinality of a vertex set inducing a graph of maximum degree at most one. **The independence–dissociation conjecture.** One has

$$
\alpha(G)\geq \frac{5}{8}{\rm diss}(G)-\frac{1}{4}.
$$

The conjecture proposes a sharp factor for comparing the independence number and dissociation number in triangle-free subcubic graphs; the stated bound is not established in the supplied source context.
record.source_name: Felix Bock, Johannes Pardey, Lucia D. Penso and Dieter Rautenbach, “Relating the independence number and the dissociation number”, arXiv:2205.03404 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.03404

record.title: The maximum-density conjecture for \operatorname{PSL}_2(q) on the Kneser graph K(q+1,3)
record.statement: Let $q$ be a prime power with $q\equiv 3\pmod{4}$, and consider the Kneser graph $K(q+1,3)$ and its automorphism group. **Maximum-density conjecture.** The group $\operatorname{PSL}_2(q)$ gives the maximum intersection density among all subgroups of the automorphism group of $K(q+1,3)$. Moreover, if $q^2\equiv 1\pmod{5}$, then the intersection density of $K(q+1,3)$ is $4/3$, while if $q^2\equiv 4\pmod{5}$, it is $1$. The claim would identify both an extremal group and the resulting density in the two congruence cases.
record.source_name: Karen Meagher and Andriaherimanana Sarobidy Razafimahatratra, “On the intersection density of the Kneser Graph K(n,3)”, arXiv:2205.05118 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.05118

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of May 2022). “The group $\mathieu{11}(12)$ has intersection density 1 (this was verified by determining that the maximum coclique in the subgraph of the derangement graph induced by the non-neighbours of the identity has size $35$.”

record.title: Finite-size correction conjecture for longest increasing subsequences
record.statement:
Let $l_N^\square$ be the length of the longest increasing subsequence in the finite $N$ model, and let $E_2^{\rm soft}(0;(t,\infty))$ denote the soft-edge limiting distribution. Set

$$
F_{2,0}(t)=E_2^{\rm soft}(0;(t,\infty)).
$$

Here $t^*$ is the rescaled variable defined in the source's equation (1.1i). **Finite-size correction conjecture.** For some function $F_{2,1}(t)$,

$$
\Pr\left(\frac{l_N^\square-2\sqrt{N}}{N^{1/6}}\leq t\right)=F_{2,0}(t^*)+\frac{1}{N^{1/3}}F_{2,1}(t)+\cdots.
$$

This conjectures the first finite-$N$ correction to the limiting soft-edge law. The preceding discussion states that the available Poissonized asymptotics do not determine this correction and that the formula is supported by numerical methods.
record.source_name: Peter J. Forrester and Anthony Mays, “Finite size corrections relating to distributions of the length of longest increasing subsequences”, arXiv:2205.05257 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.05257

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2022).

record.title: Vanishing algebraic connectivity for regular graphs
record.statement:
For $d\geq 1$, let the maximum range over all $2d$-regular graphs $G$ on $n$ vertices be taken. **Regular-graph vanishing conjecture.**

$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}\max\{a_d(G):\,G\text{ is $2d$-regular on $n$ vertices}\}=0.
$$

This is presented as a possible generalization of a conjecture attributed in the source to Jordan. It is motivated by computer calculations, but the source gives no proof or resolution.
record.source_name: Alan Lew, Eran Nevo, Yuval Peled and Orit E. Raz, “On the d-dimensional algebraic connectivity of graphs”, arXiv:2205.05530 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.05530

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2022).

record.title: Cross Gramian coherence lower-bound conjecture for dual frames
record.statement:
Let $F$ be a frame for $\mathbb{F}^n$, and let $G$ be one of its dual frames. Write $Gr(F,G)$ for their cross Gramian and let $\mu(Gr(F,G))$ denote its maximum off-diagonal magnitude. **Cross Gramian lower-bound conjecture.**

$$
\mu(Gr(F,G)) \geq \sqrt{\frac{nk-n^2}{k^2(k-1)}}.
$$

The paper gives a partial proof, but notes that one of the cases needed for the argument does not occur in its examples; the conjecture is therefore not established in full.
record.source_name: Roza Aceska and McKenna Kaczanowski, “Cross Frame Potential”, arXiv:2205.05613 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.05613

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2022).

record.title: The planar total-domination conjecture for minimum degree three
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a planar graph, let $d_t(G)$ denote its total domatic number, and let the **minimum degree** of $G$ be the least degree of any vertex. **Planar total-domination conjecture.** If $G$ has minimum degree at least three, then

$$
d_t(G)\geq 2.
$$

This assertion extends the near-triangulation result to all planar graphs of minimum degree at least three. The source presents it among the authors' proposed conjectures and does not report a resolution.
record.source_name: P. Francis, Abraham M. Illickan, Lijo M. Jose and Deepak Rajendraprasad, “Disjoint Total Dominating Sets in Near-Triangulations”, arXiv:2205.06464 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.06464

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2022). “This conjecture is still open.”

record.title: The comparison conjecture for the $2/2$- and $3/3$-powers
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with maximum degree $\Delta(G)\geq 2$. For positive integers $m,n$, $G^{\frac{m}{n}}$ denotes the $m$-power of the $n$-subdivision of $G$; in particular, $G^{\frac{2}{2}}$ and $G^{\frac{3}{3}}$ are the corresponding fractional powers, and $\chi$ denotes chromatic number. **Fractional-power comparison conjecture.**

$$
\chi(G^{\frac{2}{2}})\leq\chi(G^{\frac{3}{3}}).
$$

The source presents this as a consequence that would follow if the total coloring conjecture were correct, and attributes it to the cited work of Mahsa. Its general status is not resolved in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Mahsa Mozafari-Nia and Moharram N. Iradmusa, “Simultaneous coloring of vertices and incidences of graphs”, arXiv:2205.07189 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.07189

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2022).

record.title: The exact square coloring conjecture for planar graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a planar graph with maximum degree $Delta$. The **exact square coloring conjecture.** asserts

$$
\chi^{\#2}(G)=\left\lfloor\frac{3}{2}\Delta\right\rfloor.
$$

Here $chi^{\#2}(G)$ is the exact square chromatic number, where conflicts occur only between vertices at distance exactly $2$. The source contrasts this with injective coloring, for which triangles create conflicts, and gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Hoang La and Kenny Štorgel, “2-distance, injective, and exact square list-coloring of planar graphs with maximum degree 4”, arXiv:2205.07968 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.07968

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2022).

record.title: The iterative surface-Hadamard conjecture for the semiclassical Yukawa model
record.statement: Let $\chi$ be the classical scalar field, let $\omega_{\mathcal C}$ be an initial state on an initial surface $\mathcal C$, and consider the three 3-smeared initial two-point functions of the quantum field and its momentum. **Yukawa iterative conjecture.** At the $k$th stage, conditions on these initial two-point functions depend only on the values of $\chi$ and its derivatives through order $k-2$, determined at earlier stages, and determine the $(k+1)$st time derivative of $\chi$. This conjecture is the basis for defining surface Hadamard initial states through an infinite iterative process; the paper does not prove the asserted continuation of the process.
record.source_name: Benito A. Juárez-Aubry, Bernard S. Kay, Tonatiuh Miramontes and Daniel Sudarsky, “On the initial value problem for semiclassical gravity without and with quantum state collapses”, arXiv:2205.11671 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.11671

record.title: The projective-dimension conjecture for edge rings with 2-linear resolutions
record.statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a graph, let $n=|V|$, and let $k[G]=k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/I(G)$ be its edge ring, where $I(G)$ is generated by $\{x_ix_j:\{i,j\}\in E\}$. Write $\operatorname{pd}(k[G])$ for the projective dimension of $k[G]$, and let the maximal degree of a vertex in $G$ mean the maximum of the vertex degrees. **The edge-ring projective-dimension conjecture.** If $k[G]$ has a 2-linear resolution, then

$$
\operatorname{pd}(k[G])=\max_{v\in V}\deg_G(v).
$$

The conjecture relates the homological complexity of an edge ring to the maximum vertex degree of its graph. In the supplied source, it is presented as the conjecture being treated; the provided material gives no resolution status beyond the paper’s title, so its database status is recorded as open.
record.source_name: Ralf Fröberg, “Solution to a conjecture on edge rings with 2-linear resolutions”, arXiv:2205.14436 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.14436

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of May 2022); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Conjecture on edge coloring signed complete bipartite graphs with equal parts
record.statement:
Let $r \in \mathbf{N}$ and let $S$ be a signed complete bipartite graph $K_{r,r}$. Write $\chi'(S)$ for its signed edge-chromatic number and $\Delta(S)$ for its maximum degree. **Signed complete-bipartite edge-coloring conjecture.** If either $r$ is odd, or $r$ is even and $S$ has an even number of negative edges, then

$$
\chi'(S)=\Delta(S).
$$

The conjecture complements the obstruction for even $r$ when the graph has an odd number of negative edges; the latter cannot be colored with $\Delta(S)$ colors. Its truth would also imply the stated perfect-matching and $2$-regular-decomposition property for the odd-$r$ case. No resolution is given here.
record.source_name: Robert Janczewski, Krzysztof Turowski and Bartłomiej Wróblewski, “Edge coloring of graphs of signed class 1 and 2”, arXiv:2205.15425 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.15425

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2022).

record.title: The conjecture for $\mathbf{Q}_{m,n}^{k}(1)$
record.statement:
Let $M$ and $N$ be positive integers, and define

$$
k=\gcd(M,N),\qquad m=M/k,\qquad n=N/k.
$$

Let $L_{M,N}$ be the symmetric function associated with the $M,N$-path tuples, let $\mathbf{Q}_{m,n}$ be the elliptic Hall algebra operator, and let $\operatorname{pdinv}(\bm{P})$ denote the path statistic used in the definition of $L_{M,N}$. Define $C$ by

$$
C=\max_{\bm{P}}\operatorname{pdinv}(\bm{P}),
$$

where the maximum is over all $M,N$-path tuples $\bm{P}$. **The conjecture for $\mathbf{Q}_{m,n}^{k}(1)$.** One has

$$
\mathbf{Q}_{m,n}^{k}(1)=\pm(1-q)^k t^C L_{M,N}.
$$

This is the paper's main conjecture, relating the elliptic Hall algebra expression to the lattice-path symmetric function; the supplied material does not state whether it has been resolved.
record.source_name: Andy Wilson, “A symmetric function lift of torus link homology”, arXiv:2206.00075 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.00075

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of June 2022). “This conjecture was proved by Mellit .”

record.title: The cubic hypergraph bootstrap quadratic running-time conjecture
record.statement:
Let $M_4^3(n)$ be the maximum running time of the $K_4^3$-bootstrap process over all initial $3$-uniform hypergraphs on $n$ vertices. The paper gives a quadratic lower bound for this process. **Quadratic running-time conjecture.**

$$
M_4^3(n)=O(n^2).
$$

Together with the paper's quadratic lower bound, this would determine the running time up to a constant factor. The supplied text does not state a resolution.
record.source_name: Jonathan A. Noel and Arjun Ranganathan, “On the Running Time of Hypergraph Bootstrap Percolation”, arXiv:2206.02940 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.02940

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of June 2022). “This was disproved for all $k\geq6$ by Balogh, Kronenberg, Pokrovskiy and Szab\'o .”

record.title: Cvetković–Rowlinson–Simić conjecture on the signless Laplacian spread
record.statement:
Let $s_Q(G)$ denote the difference between the largest and least eigenvalues of the signless Laplacian of a graph $G$. Let $K_{n-1}^+$ be the graph obtained by adding a pendant edge to the complete graph $K_{n-1}$; let $P_n$ and $C_n$ denote the path and cycle on $n$ vertices, respectively.

**Cvetković–Rowlinson–Simić conjecture.** Over all connected graphs on $n\geq6$ vertices, $s_Q(G)$ is maximized by $K_{n-1}^+$ and minimized by $P_n$ and, when $n$ is odd, by $C_n$.

The minimizing assertion was proved independently by Das and by Fan et al. The maximizing assertion was confirmed in this paper for sufficiently large $n$.
record.source_name: Lele Liu, “Two conjectures in spectral graph theory involving the linear combinations of graph eigenvalues”, arXiv:2206.03723 (2022).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2017–2022). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1709.00182](https://arxiv.org/abs/1709.00182).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.03723

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of June 2022). “It is worth mentioning that the second part of Conjecture was proved by Das and Fan et al. independently using different proof techniques.”

record.title: Vertex attainment conjecture for the distance-to-conformal-radius ratio
record.statement:
Let $P$ be a bounded convex $n$-gon, decomposed into regions $P_j$ consisting of points closer to the $j$-th side than to the other sides. Let $Gr(P)$ be the resulting graph after removing the boundary points of $P$ and the open edges having nonempty intersection with $\partial P$. For $u\in P$, write $d_P(u)$ for the distance to the boundary and $r_P(u)$ for the conformal radius.

**Vertex attainment conjecture.** The maximum

$$
\max_{u\in P}\frac{2d_P(u)}{r_P(u)}
$$

is attained at a vertex of the graph $Gr(P)$. This is stronger than the preceding theorem, which only guarantees attainment at some point of $Gr(P)$. The conjecture concerns sharp localization of the extremum for convex polygonal domains and remains unresolved in the supplied source.
record.source_name: D. Dautova, R. Kargar, S. Nasyrov and M. Vuorinen, “Intrinsic metrics in polygonal domains”, arXiv:2206.03744 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.03744

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2022).

record.title: The graph complement conjecture for minimum rank and maximum nullity
record.statement:
For a graph $G$ on $n$ vertices, let $S(G)$ be the set of real symmetric matrices whose off-diagonal zero pattern is prescribed by adjacency in $G$. Define $mr(G)$ as the minimum rank of a matrix in $S(G)$ and $M(G)=n-mr(G)$ as the maximum nullity. **Graph complement conjecture.** For any graph $G$, 
$$
mr(G)+mr(\overline{G})\leq |G|+2
$$
 and equivalently 
$$
M(G)+M(\overline{G})\geq |G|-2.
$$
 This conjecture gives equivalent formulations in terms of minimum rank and maximum nullity for a graph and its complement; the source presents it as a possible future direction, but the supplied text does not establish its resolution.
record.source_name: Emelie Curl, Shaun Fallat, Ryan Moruzzi, Carolyn Reinhart and Derek Young, “On the zero forcing number of the complement of graphs with forbidden subgraphs”, arXiv:2206.03932 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.03932

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2022).

record.title: The winding-number lower-bound conjecture for satellite knots
record.statement:
Let $K$ be a satellite of a nontrivial knot, and let the pattern have winding number $p$. The unknotting number $u(K)$ is the minimum number of crossing changes needed to transform $K$ into the unknot.

**Winding-number lower-bound conjecture.**

$$
u(K) \geq p+1.
$$

This would generalize the result of Scharlemann and Thompson that a nontrivial satellite with nonzero winding number has unknotting number at least $2$. The conjecture proposes a stronger lower bound in terms of the pattern's winding number; its status is not resolved in the source.
record.source_name: Jennifer Hom, Tye Lidman and JungHwan Park, “Unknotting number and cabling”, arXiv:2206.04196 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.04196

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2022).

record.title: Inherited correspondence between disjoint cycles and non-zero eigenvalues
record.statement:
Let $G=([n],E)$ be a directed graph, and let $0 \leq k \leq n$ be an integer. For a subgraph $H$ of $G$, consider collections of disjoint cycles in $H$, and let $\mathcal{S}_G$ denote the associated matrix space.

**Inherited correspondence conjecture.** The maximum number of edges in a subgraph $H$ of $G$ in which every collection of disjoint cycles covers at most $k$ vertices equals the largest dimension of a subspace of $\mathcal{S}_G$ in which every matrix has at most $k$ non-zero eigenvalues.

This conjecture seeks to strengthen the established correspondence between collections of disjoint cycles and the non-zero eigenvalues of matrices in $\mathcal{S}_G$. Its proof or disproof is identified by the authors as an interesting open problem.
record.source_name: Yinan Li, Youming Qiao, Avi Wigderson, Yuval Wigderson and Chuanqi Zhang, “Connections between graphs and matrix spaces”, arXiv:2206.04815 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.04815

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2022).

record.title: The even-like extremal binary LCD code conjecture
record.statement:
Let $k$ be an even positive integer and let $n>k$ be an integer. Write $d_2^{E}(n,k)$ for the relevant extremal minimum distance of binary LCD codes, and call a binary LCD code **even-like** when every codeword has even Hamming weight. **The even-like extremal-code conjecture.** If $d_2^{E}(n,k)$ is even and

$$
d_2^{E}(n-1,k)=d_2^{E}(n,k)-1,
$$

then every binary LCD $[n,k,d_2^{E}(n,k)]$ code is even-like. The paper states that this conjecture is invalid and provides two counterexamples.
record.source_name: Shitao Li, Minjia Shi and Huizhou Liu, “Several constructions of optimal LCD codes over small finite fields”, arXiv:2206.04936 (2023).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2020–2022). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2010.13399](https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.13399).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.04936

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of June 2022); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “refuted”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Existence of a knot with incompatible stick number and superbridge index realizations
record.statement: Let $K$ be a knot type. Its **stick number** is the minimum number of edges in a polygonal realization of $K$, denoted by $\operatorname{stick}[K]$, and its **superbridge index** is the minimum superbridge number over all realizations of $K$, denoted by $\operatorname{sb}[K]$. **Incompatibility conjecture.** There exists a knot type $K$ for which no polygonal realization achieves both $\operatorname{stick}[K]$ and $\operatorname{sb}[K]$. The possibility is suggested by examples of knots whose known stick-number-minimizing realizations do not also realize their superbridge index, but the existence of such a knot remains open.
record.source_name: Clayton Shonkwiler, “New Superbridge Index Calculations from Non-Minimal Realizations”, arXiv:2206.06950 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.06950

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2022).

record.title: Minimality conjecture for defect subgroups of contragredient quasireductive supergroups
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a quasireductive supergroup whose Lie superalgebra $\operatorname{Lie}G$ is contragredient. A **defect subgroup** $D$ of $G$ is a subgroup associated with the defect of the contragredient Lie superalgebra, and a **splitting subgroup** is a quasireductive subgroup satisfying the splitting condition for $G$.

**Minimality conjecture.** Up to conjugacy, a defect subgroup $D$ of $G$ is the unique minimal splitting subgroup.

The claim identifies the defect subgroup as the smallest splitting subgroup, modulo conjugacy, under the stated contragredient hypothesis. The supplied text gives no evidence that this conjecture has been resolved.
record.source_name: Vera Serganova and Alexander Sherman, “Splitting quasireductive supergroups and volumes of supergrassmannians”, arXiv:2206.07693 (2023).

record.title: Prime-folding characterization of extremal tensors
record.statement:
Let $2\le n=\prod_{k=1}^{s_n}p_k$ be the prime factorization, with $2\le p_1\le p_2\le\dots\le p_{s_n}$. Consider a tensor $\mathcal{T}\in\mathbb{B}^{p_1\times p_2\times\dots\times p_{s_n}\times p_1\times p_2\times\dots\times p_{s_n}}$, where $\mathbb{B}$ denotes the set of zero-one tensors. **Prime-folding conjecture.** If $\mathcal{T}$ satisfies

$$
\|\mathcal{T}\|_\sigma=1\quad\text{and}\quad\|\mathcal{T}\|=\sqrt{n},
$$

then $\mathcal{T}$ can be unfolded to a permutation matrix in $\mathbb{B}^{n\times n}$. This is the remaining structural step toward the preceding characterization conjecture, after reducing to maximum foldings with prime mode dimensions; the paper explicitly says that it cannot currently prove this assertion.

record.title: The maximum-degree phase-transition conjecture for optimal resistor networks
record.statement:
Consider optimal graphs with a prescribed average degree and $n$ vertices. Write $\Omega(n)$ for a quantity bounded below by a positive constant times $n$, and $o(n)$ for a quantity whose ratio to $n$ tends to zero.

**Maximum-degree phase-transition conjecture.** There is a threshold $\alpha_1$ on the average degree such that below it an optimal graph has a vertex of degree $\Omega(n)$, whereas above it all vertices have degree $o(n)$.

This is a second proposed phase transition between star-like and regular-like behaviour, addressing concentration of edges at high-degree vertices rather than merely the presence of leaves. Its status remains open in the source.

record.title: The motivated de Rham–Betti conjecture
record.statement:
Let $M$ be an André motive over $K$, and let $Z_M$ be the Zariski closure of its comparison isomorphism, $\Omega_M$ the smallest $K$-subtorsor generated by that comparison, $\Omega_M^{\mathrm{dRB}}$ the torsor of de Rham–Betti periods, and $\Omega_M^{\mathrm{And}}$ the torsor of motivated periods. **The motivated de Rham–Betti conjecture.** The inclusions

$$
Z_M\subseteq\Omega_M\subseteq\Omega_M^{\mathrm{dRB}}\subseteq\Omega_M^{\mathrm{And}}
$$

are equalities. This is the motivated version of Grothendieck's period conjecture for André motives; the source states that the general conjecture is unresolved.

record.title: Ramanujan–Hardy–Littlewood conjecture for the Möbius function
record.statement:
Let $\rho$ range over the non-trivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function $\zeta(s)$. Let $b[?25l\alpha$ and $\beta$ be positive real numbers satisfying

$$
\alpha\beta=\pi.
$$

Assume that the series

$$
\sum_{\rho}\frac{\Gamma\left(\frac{1-\rho}{2}\right)}{\zeta'(\rho)}x^{\rho}
$$

converges for every positive real $x$, and that all non-trivial zeros of $\zeta(s)$ are simple. **Ramanujan–Hardy–Littlewood conjecture.** Under these assumptions,

$$
\sqrt{\alpha}\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{\mu(n)}{n}e^{-\alpha^2/n^2}-\sqrt{\beta}\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{\mu(n)}{n}e^{-\beta^2/n^2}=-\frac{1}{2\sqrt{\beta}}\sum_{\rho}\frac{\Gamma\left(\frac{1-\rho}{2}\right)}{\zeta'(\rho)}\beta^{\rho}.
$$

This is a corrected modular transformation involving infinite series of the Möbius function and the non-trivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function. The source states that it has not been proved rigorously; the displayed identity is conditional on the stated convergence and simplicity assumptions.

record.title: Gouvêa–Mazur conjecture on local constancy of slopes
record.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime number, let $N$ be a positive integer coprime to $p$, and normalize the $p$-adic valuation on $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_p$ by $v_p(p)=1$. For $r\in\mathbb{Q}$ and a space $S$ of modular forms with $U_p$-action, let $d(S,r)$ be the number of generalized eigenvalues of $U_p$ with $p$-adic valuation $r$. Let $S_k(\Gamma_0(Np))$ be the space of cusp forms of weight $k$ and level $Np$. **Gouvêa–Mazur conjecture.** The polynomial $M(x)$ in the preceding local-constancy statement can be chosen as $M(x)=x$; equivalently, for every $r\in\mathbb{Q}_{\geq 0}$, if $k_1,k_2$ are integers satisfying

$$
k_1\geq 2r+2,\qquad k_2\geq 2r+2,
$$

and

$$
k_1\equiv k_2\pmod{(p-1)p^m}
$$

for an integer $m\geq r$, then

$$
d\left(S_{k_1}(\Gamma_0(Np)),r\right)=d\left(S_{k_2}(\Gamma_0(Np)),r\right).
$$

The conjecture concerns the local constancy of slopes of modular forms as the weight varies $p$-adically. Buzzard and Calegari disproved it by giving an explicit counterexample, so the claim is refuted.
record.source_name: Rufei Ren, “Localized Gouvêa-Mazur conjecture”, arXiv:2206.11577 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.11577

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of June 2022). “In , Buzzard and Calegari disproved this conjecture by giving an explicit counterexample.”

record.title: Improved upper bounds for Staller–Maker–Breaker domination numbers
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices, with minimum degree $\delta(G)$. The S-game and D-game parameters are denoted by $\gamma_{\rm SMB}'(G)$ and $\gamma_{\rm SMB}(G)$, respectively.

**Improved SMBD-number bounds.**

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\text{(i) If }\gamma_{\rm SMB}'(G)<\infty,\text{ then }\gamma_{\rm SMB}'(G)\le \left\lceil\frac{n}{2}\right\rceil-\delta(G)+1;\\
&\text{(ii) If }\gamma_{\rm SMB}(G)<\infty,\text{ then }\gamma_{\rm SMB}(G)\le \left\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\right\rfloor-\delta(G)+1.
\end{aligned}
$$

These bounds would improve the known sharp general upper bounds when the minimum degree is at least two; the authors note that sharp examples under this degree condition are not known.
record.source_name: Csilla Bujtás and Pakanun Dokyeesun, “Fast winning strategies for Staller in the Maker-Breaker domination game”, arXiv:2206.12812 (2022).
record.references:

record.title: Henning et al.'s conjectured upper bound for minimum total dominating sets in trees
record.statement:
Let $T$ be a tree of order $n\geq 2$, with total domination number $\gamma_t$, and let $\Gamma_t(T)$ denote the number of minimum total dominating sets of $T$. **Henning et al.'s conjectured upper bound.** One should have

$$
\Gamma_t(T) \leq \left(\frac{n-\frac{\gamma_t}{2}}{\frac{\gamma_t}{2}}\right)^\frac{\gamma_t}{2}.
$$

The paper presents this as a proposed upper bound motivated by conjectured extremal examples; the supplied text does not state whether it is proved or disproved.

record.title: Belfiore–Solé secrecy function conjecture for formally unimodular lattices
record.statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a formally unimodular lattice, and let $\Xi_{\Lambda}(\tau)$ denote its secrecy function and $\xi_{\Lambda}$ its maximum value. **Belfiore–Solé secrecy function conjecture.** The secrecy function achieves its maximum at $\tau=1$, i.e.,

$$
\xi_{\Lambda}=\Xi_{\Lambda}(1).
$$
 This conjecture concerns the weak secrecy symmetry point of formally unimodular lattices and is the lattice version of the secrecy gain conjecture introduced by Belfiore and Solé.

record.title: Secrecy function conjecture for formally unimodular packings
record.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a formally unimodular packing, and let $\Xi_{\Gamma}(\tau)$ denote its secrecy function and $\xi_{\Gamma}$ its maximum value. **Formally unimodular packing secrecy function conjecture.** The secrecy function achieves its maximum at $\tau=1$, i.e.,

$$
\xi_{\Gamma}=\Xi_{\Gamma}(1).
$$
 This is the generalized packing version of the formally unimodular lattice conjecture. The source presents it as the basis for studying secrecy-optimal Construction A packings.

record.title: The cubic graph girth bound conjecture
record.statement:
Let $g(n)$ denote the largest girth among all cubic graphs on $n$ vertices. **Girth bound conjecture.** There is a constant $\epsilon_0>0$ such that

$$
(2-\epsilon_0)\log_2 n \ge g(n).
$$

The Moore bound gives only $g(n)\leq (2+o_n(1))\log_2 n$, while the best known lower bound is greater than $\frac{4}{3}\log_2 n-2$ for infinitely many explicitly constructed graphs. The conjecture proposes a uniform improvement to the leading constant in the upper bound.

record.title: The ionization conjecture for atoms
record.statement:
Let $H_N$ be the $N$-electron atomic Hamiltonian with nuclear charge $Z\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $E_N=\inf\sigma(H_N)$. Denote by $N_c=N_c(Z)$ the largest number of electrons for which $E_{N_c}$ has a minimizer. **Ionization conjecture.** There is a constant $C>0$, possibly $C=1$, such that

$$
N_c\leqslant Z+C.
$$

The existence of minimizers for $N<Z+1$ is known by Zhislin's theorem, while the uniform bound on the number of excess electrons remains open.
record.source_name: Phan Thành Nam, “The ionization problem in quantum mechanics”, arXiv:2206.15393 (2022).

record.title: Ahanjideh–Ekim–Yıldız conjecture for intermediate triangle-free extremal values
record.statement:
For natural numbers $d$ and $i$, let $f_{\vartriangle}(d,i)$ be the maximum number of edges in a triangle-free graph with maximum degree at most $d$ and matching number at most $i$. Let $Z(d)$ be the largest matching number of the factor-critical, almost regular, triangle-free graph used in the paper's decomposition of edge-extremal graphs.

**Intermediate-value conjecture.** For $7\leq d<i<Z(d)$,

$$
f_{\vartriangle}(d,i)=di+i-d+1.
$$

This conjecture supplies the missing values of $f_{\vartriangle}(d,i)$ between $d$ and $Z(d)$ and is intended to imply the paper's general formula for $f_{\vartriangle}(d,m)$. These intermediate cases are left open in the paper.
record.source_name: Milad Ahanjideh, Tınaz Ekim and Mehmet Akif Yıldız, “Maximum size of a triangle-free graph with bounded maximum degree and matching number”, arXiv:2207.02271 (2022).

record.title: Ahanjideh–Ekim–Yıldız general formula for triangle-free extremal graphs in terms of $Z(d)$
record.statement:
Let $d$ and $m$ be natural numbers, let $Z(d)$ be the parameter defined by the largest matching number of the relevant factor-critical triangle-free graph, and write

$$
m=kZ(d)+r,\qquad 0\leq r<Z(d).
$$

Let $f_{\vartriangle}(d,m)$ denote the maximum number of edges in a triangle-free graph with maximum degree at most $d$ and matching number at most $m$.

**General formula in terms of $Z(d)$.**

$$
f_{\vartriangle}(d,m)=
\begin{cases}
 dm+k\left\lfloor d/2\right\rfloor,& r<d,\\
 dm+k\left\lfloor d/2\right\rfloor+r-d+1,& r\geq d.
\end{cases}
$$

The formula is presented as a consequence of the intermediate-value conjecture and would extend the theorem to all integers $d$ and $m$. Thus it remains conjectural whenever that preceding conjecture is unresolved.

record.title: Herzog–Kaplan–Lev product-length conjecture for cycle classes
record.statement:
Let $n(k,l)$ be the largest integer $n$ such that every element of the alternating group $A_n$ is a product of $k$ many $l$-cycles, where $k,l\geq 2$ and either $l$ is odd or $k$ is even. **Herzog–Kaplan–Lev conjecture.**

$$
\left\lfloor\frac{2}{3}kl\right\rfloor\leq n(k,l)\leq \left\lfloor\frac{2}{3}kl\right\rfloor+1.
$$

This conjecture generalizes known results on products of cycle classes; it was verified in several cases, including $3\mid l$, $l\geq 9$, and odd $l$, but remains open in general.
record.source_name: Harish Kishnani, Rijubrata Kundu and Sumit Chandra Mishra, “Alternating groups as products of cycle classes”, arXiv:2207.03165 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.03165

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2022). “Thompson's conjecture has been proved for a large number of finite simple groups, although it remains open for infinite family of groups.”
